newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: COLOSSAL STARTS ZAMBIAN COBALT PRODUCTION.
newsitem.headline: COLOSSAL STARTS ZAMBIAN COBALT PRODUCTION.

text.p: Colossal Resource Corp has started cobalt production from Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) slag in the central town of Kabwe, the company's Zambia representative said on Wednesday.
Nic Money, managing director of the Colossal-owned Qasim Mining Enterprises Ltd (QMEL) said the company started limited sales of cobalt material late last year.
"Our first sale of about 12 tonnes of alloy was made to South Africa in November. We will make a second sale this month and a third by February," Money told Reuters.
Money said the first alloy produced at Kabwe had been granulated -- refined from around six to eight percent cobalt to about 15 percent -- in South Africa.

The second alloy would also be treated in South Africa, but the company intended to instal an induction melting furnace at its Kabwe plant before the end of January to enable it granulate subsequent alloys locally.
"We expect to commission the induction melting furnace by January 20," he said.
The company currently processes ZCCM slag with an average cobalt content of 0.8 percent, to up to eight percent.
It expects to process between 4,000 and 6,000 tonnes of slag per month in its first year, producing around 50 tonnes of cobalt material per month.
Money said the company was working on developing a hydro-metallurgical facility to enable it procees slag to 99 percent cobalt content.
"This technology many come into operation within the next three years," he said.
The company had spent around $9 million in capital costs at the Kabwe plant and expected to put in around $8 million more.
